clue.text: Bloke, from our perspective, has a point — it's forbidden by commandment

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a bloke or chap
a view held from our perspective is one that seems so to us
a ness is a headland or promontory, a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A man with his own viewpoint makes a point about something the Ten Commandments forbid.
explanation.walkthrough: The tenth commandment forbids coveting a neighbour's goods; COVE is old British slang for a man, and NESS is found in coastal place names for a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth commandment, 'Thou shalt not covet', bans greedy desire for what belongs to others.

clue.text: Pot with small diameter or depth

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal English for small
D is the standard abbreviation for both diameter and depth

explanation.surface: A cooking pot with a modest width or depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang names for cannabis, the drug smoked in a joint.

clue.text: Deity is depicted by old master, so-called

parts.note: sir is a respectful address to a master or schoolmaster

explanation.surface: A god as portrayed in the painting of a so-called Old Master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' suggests a great painter, but it splits into O and SIR; 'depicted by' places IS after them, and 'so-called' merely says that this is what the pieces are called.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian god of the underworld and the dead, husband of Isis.

clue.text: Newspaper feature used by phrenologist?

definitions.meaning: the large-type title over a press story
a phrenologist reads character from the head, so a line on the head would be his tool, whimsically

explanation.definitionFit: A banner title tops a press story, while a crease across the skull would be a reading for a head-studying quack.

clue.text: Vice as result of consuming passion

definitions.meaning: one of the seven deadly sins
a passion for consuming, that is eating, leads to greed for food

explanation.definitionFit: Overeating is one of the seven deadly sins, and a passion for consuming food is exactly what produces it.

clue.text: Finds out how sectarians may be converted

indicators.note: converted letters are changed into a new form, signalling that sectarians is rearranged

explanation.surface: Discovers how religious zealots might be won over to another faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suits sectarians and religious conversion, but it signals that the letters of SECTARIANS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine or establish a fact is to discover it for certain.

clue.text: Fail to rise as expected

parts.note: reads like a cake or bread that will not puff up, but means staying in bed past the alarm

explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping beyond the intended waking time is failing to get up when planned.

clue.text: Wild animals collectively under pressure, fairground attraction

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a ride such as a roller coaster or carousel is a fairground attraction

explanation.surface: Beasts kept under strain as a funfair attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' is a link here, P simply coming before RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a group of lions is this word.

clue.text: Sensuality depicted in illustrations

indicators.note: something depicted in the word illustrations is shown within its letters

explanation.definitionFit: Strong sexual desire is a carnal, sensual appetite.

clue.text: Tree more mature than little ones in nursery

definitions.meaning: a shrub or small tree with white flowers and dark berries

definitions.text: more mature than little ones in nursery
definitions.meaning: older than the small children in a nursery

explanation.definitionFit: Sambucus is a small tree with edible berries; the comparative of old describes one born earlier than the young.

clue.text: Most delicate one protected by US lawyer in trial

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed and shielded within it

parts.note: a test is a trial
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fragile person is shielded by an American attorney during a court trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' suggests a courtroom alongside the lawyer, but means TEST; 'protected by' puts I inside it to make TIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word for fine, dainty and fragile.

clue.text: Help with one's bags hotel may provide

definitions.text: Help with one's bags hotel may provide

parts.words: Help with one's bags hotel may provide
parts.note: sounds like a porter carrying luggage, but bags are baggy trousers needing creases

explanation.definitionFit: A hotel bedroom gadget smooths the creases in a guest's slacks.

clue.text: Awful bosses I have, given to micro-management

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: VE is the contracted form of have, as in I've

explanation.surface: A grumble that one's dreadful managers constantly interfere in small details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges BOSSES and I to make OBSESSI, and VE from 'have' completes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cannot stop controlling every small detail is fixated and compulsive.

clue.text: Money in the form of royalty

definitions.meaning: old British gold coins worth one pound

explanation.definitionFit: These gold coins were worth one pound each, and the word also means monarchs who reign.

clue.text: Perform better than Manchester side in scoreless draw

indicators.note: the Manchester side sits in the middle of the scoreless draw

parts.note: a scoreless draw is nil-nil, two zeros or two Os
UTD is the abbreviation for United, as in Manchester United football club

explanation.surface: A Manchester football team plays better than expected in a goalless game.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United is a famous English football club, usually abbreviated UTD.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or exceed is to beat a rival's performance.

clue.text: Evil, say, twice ends badly in these major offences

indicators.note: badly arranged letters are in a poor order, so they are shuffled
twice says the word ends is used two times in the pool

explanation.surface: Wickedness, so to speak, comes to a bad end in these grave sins.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is EVIL, SAY and ENDS twice; 'badly' rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride, greed, lust, envy, gluttony, wrath and sloth are the gravest sins of Christian teaching.

clue.text: No states protecting, for example, these groups of flowers

indicators.note: the states piece wraps around the example abbreviation to protect it

parts.note: says means states or declares
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: No countries are guarding these bunches of blooms, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like countries but is the verb SAYS, which closes round EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Small posies of flowers carried or worn are traditional bouquets.

clue.text: Change of direction, dropping one current article of faith

indicators.note: a change of letters means they are rearranged
dropping says a piece is taken away from the word direction

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current; one such I goes

explanation.surface: A shift in course, abandoning one prevailing tenet of belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes one I (current) from DIRECTION, leaving DRECTION, and 'Change of' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet or creed is a principle that a religion teaches its believers.

clue.text: Ready in many countries to emerge from neuroses

indicators.note: the letters emerge from inside the word neuroses

explanation.surface: Someone prepared to leave behind their anxieties abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash, here the money used across many European nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The single currency of most EU nations is the cash spent across those countries.

clue.text: Next man coming in hit zero runs

parts.note: a hit is a success
O resembles zero
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: In cricket, the next batsman in struck a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next man coming in' and 'runs' paint a cricket scene, the next batsman, but the definition is one who takes over a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows another in an office or role is the heir to it.

clue.text: Peaceful creature reluctant to join second …

indicators.note: the reluctant piece comes to join on after the second

parts.note: loth is a variant spelling of loath, meaning reluctant

explanation.surface: A calm animal is unwilling to take part in another round.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue; it is a surface device only.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow tree-hanging mammal of South America is famously placid and idle.

clue.text: … and others in retaliation

indicators.note: the letters sit in the word retaliation

explanation.surface: Other people join in getting their own back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase abbreviated et al. means and other people.

clue.text: Way in which spring often draws to a close

definitions.text: Way in which spring often draws to a close

parts.words: Way in which spring often draws to a close
parts.note: sounds like the season ending, but means an entrance whose coiled spring pulls it shut

explanation.definitionFit: A door on hinges with a spring that pulls it shut is an entrance that closes itself.

clue.text: Retrospective emotion of 50's drama

parts.note: John Osborne's 1956 play Look Back in ... names a feeling viewed in retrospect

explanation.walkthrough: Look Back in Anger is a famous 1956 British play by John Osborne; 'Retrospective' stands for 'Look back in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's title pairs looking back with a fierce feeling of rage.

clue.text: English poet dull for Americans

definitions.meaning: Thomas ... wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
the American spelling of the colour between black and white, a dull shade

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray was an eighteenth-century writer of verse, and the US spelling names a drab colour.

clue.text: Desire shown by representative, but not love

indicators.note: but not tells us the love letter is excluded

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic representative
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Longing displayed by a delegate, but without affection.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring, love means nil, so it gives O, which comes out of ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting what another has is covetous longing.

clue.text: Get measure of horses one beats in some races

definitions.note: handicap races give horses extra weights, so these are carried in some races

parts.note: a hand is four inches, the unit for a horse's height
I is the Roman numeral one
caps means beats or outdoes

explanation.surface: Get the height of horses that one outdoes in certain races.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand is four inches, the traditional unit for measuring a horse's height.
explanation.definitionFit: Weights or penalties imposed to equalise runners feature in certain contests.
